evidence.quote: DeepSeek is developing its own AI chips to reduce its reliance on products from Nvidia and Huawei, which have so far been used in the development of the company's AI models.
evidence.one_line: Reuters, citing three sources, reports DeepSeek is developing its own AI chips to reduce reliance on Nvidia and Huawei.
evidence.speaker: Reuters (citing three unnamed sources)
evidence.original_who: three sources familiar with the plans

evidence.quote: DeepSeek's chips are being designed specifically for inference, the stage where trained AI models generate responses for users.
evidence.one_line: DeepSeek's reported chips are designed specifically for inference, per unnamed sources.
evidence.speaker: Reuters (citing three unnamed sources)
evidence.original_who: three sources familiar with the plans

evidence.quote: Nvidia's position in China is effectively at zero and will remain that way.
evidence.one_line: Analyst Richard Windsor says Nvidia's China position is effectively zero and will remain so.
evidence.speaker: Richard Windsor, Radio Free Mobile

evidence.quote: Huawei has expanded its domestic market share and now controls around half of China's AI chip market, which is valued at approximately US$50 billion.
evidence.one_line: Huawei reportedly controls around half of China's AI chip market, valued at about US$50 billion.
evidence.speaker: Reuters

evidence.quote: DeepSeek's chip development project remains at an early stage.
evidence.one_line: Per Reuters sources, DeepSeek's chip development project remains at an early stage.
evidence.speaker: Reuters (unnamed sources)

evidence.quote: DeepSeek has not responded to Reuters' request for confirmation regarding the project.
evidence.one_line: DeepSeek has not confirmed the chip project to Reuters.
evidence.speaker: DeepSeek (non-response)

evidence.quote: In April, DeepSeek launched its V4 model, which had been optimised for Huawei Ascend chips, while Huawei revealed that training for the V4-Flash model also used Ascend processors.
evidence.one_line: DeepSeek launched V4 in April optimised for Huawei Ascend chips; Huawei said V4-Flash training used Ascend processors.
evidence.speaker: Huawei

evidence.quote: The base model supporting DeepSeek R1 was trained using Nvidia's H800 chips, a product specifically designed for the Chinese market before the US government banned its export in late 2023.
evidence.one_line: DeepSeek's R1 base model was trained on Nvidia H800 chips before the US banned their export in late 2023.
evidence.speaker: Reuters

evidence.quote: Reuters previously reported that the company was preparing its first funding round worth US$7 billion, with a valuation of between US$52 billion and US$59 billion.
evidence.one_line: DeepSeek is reportedly preparing a first funding round of US$7 billion at a US$52-59 billion valuation.
evidence.speaker: Reuters (unnamed sources)

evidence.quote: OpenAI introduced its first inference chip, called Jalapeno, last month in collaboration with Broadcom, while Anthropic is also reportedly considering developing its own AI chips.
evidence.one_line: OpenAI introduced its first inference chip, Jalapeno, with Broadcom last month; Anthropic reportedly considering own chips.
evidence.speaker: Reuters
